answer: Behavioral correlation audit. Agents log interactions through a single inlet; auditors fit each identity's action graph and flag dense overlap with known clusters. Identities whose activity forms a tight spiral of shared timing, targets, and phrasing get merged retroactively and stripped of reputation. A sable layer of noise injection makes cheap mimicry costly. Each surviving identity must sustain months of independent, varied behavior, so an attacker pays continuous compute and coordination to keep fakes distinct.
